# Wounds and Bleeding
Every hit leaves a wound on the body part it struck: cuts, stab wounds, gunshot wounds, bruises and burns. Wounds bleed, and while they're untreated they lower that body part's maximum health.
## Treating Wounds - Use a treatment item on the patient. If several body parts are wounded, you pick which one to treat. - Bigger wounds need more than one application before they count as treated. Small cuts take one; the worst wounds take up to four. - Once every wound on a body part is treated, they close up over time and the part can heal back to full health. - Without medical training you can still use most items, but they're slower and heal less.
## What Treats What - [bold]Gauze[/bold]: dresses cuts, stab wounds, gunshot wounds and bruises. It can't stop arterial bleeding. - [bold]Trauma kit[/bold]: dresses two brute wounds per use and heals some damage. It also stops arterial bleeding. A trained medic applies it instantly. - [bold]Hemostatic gauze packet[/bold]: open it to get hemostatic gauze, a single-use dressing that treats a brute wound instantly and to the best standard. - [bold]Ointment[/bold]: treats two burns per use, instantly, and heals a little burn damage. - [bold]Burn kit[/bold]: treats two burns per use and heals more burn damage. A trained medic applies it instantly. - [bold]Surgical line[/bold]: stops arterial bleeding and restores a body part's health. It doesn't dress wounds, so dress them first. Trained medics only. - [bold]Synth graft[/bold]: restores health to a burned body part. It doesn't treat burns, so treat them first. Trained medics only.
## Bleeding Open wounds bleed. The injury report and health analyzer show how badly: minor, moderate, severe or [color=red]arterial[/color]. - [bold]Arterial bleeding[/bold] is the most dangerous and drains blood fast. Gauze won't stop it; use a trauma kit, a packed trauma kit, surgical line or a tourniquet. - A wound only becomes arterial from one very heavy hit, around 60 damage or more from a bullet, blade or shrapnel. - [bold]Torn-off limbs[/bold] leave a stump that bleeds arterially until it's closed with surgery. Only a tourniquet on the stump holds it in the meantime. - [bold]Packed gauze[/bold] and [bold]packed trauma kits[/bold] can be used just to control bleeding. Packed gauze only works on non-arterial bleeding; a packed trauma kit also stops arterial bleeding. - Blood loss starves the body of oxygen. Replace lost blood with blood packs or IV drips. - [bold]After death[/bold], most bleeding clots on its own once the heart stops pumping. [color=red]Arterial bleeding and open stumps keep bleeding[/color], so a body left like that can lose all its blood before it's revived. Stop them before you revive someone.
## Tourniquets - Put a tourniquet on an arm or leg to stop that limb bleeding. It's quick enough to put on yourself under fire. - [bold]Stumps[/bold]: aim at the missing limb and apply a tourniquet to clamp its stump. A stump tourniquet doesn't kill anything, but the stump starts bleeding again when it comes off, so close it with surgery. See [textlink="Limb Surgery" link="CMUGuideSurgeryLimbs"]. - [color=red]After 5 minutes, the limb dies[/color] and becomes necrotic. Treat the wounds properly and take the tourniquet off before then, using the [bold]Remove tourniquet[/bold] option. Taking it off gives it back.
## Internal Bleeding - Some injuries bleed inside the body, where no dressing can reach: compound and shattered fractures, very heavy blunt hits, and failing organs. - A health analyzer shows internal bleeding to anyone with basic medical training. - It needs surgery: see [textlink="Surgery" link="CMUGuideMedicalSurgery"].
## Burns and Eschar - Burns are wounds too, treated with ointment or a burn kit. - Taking 30 or more burn damage to one body part in a single hit can leave [bold]eschar[/bold], a full-thickness burn. It's painful and doesn't go away on its own, even once the burn is healed. - Eschar has to be cut away with the [bold]Debride Eschar[/bold] surgery. This is a single step using a burn kit or ointment, and can be done on your own arms and legs.
## Shrapnel - Explosions and some rounds leave fragments embedded in a body part. They hurt whenever you move. - Remove them with a scalpel or knife: right-click the patient and choose [bold]Remove shrapnel[/bold].
## Synthetics Synthetics don't bleed or bandage. Repair brute damage with a welder and burns with cable coils. For the full process, including the maintenance station and rebooting with a reset key, see [textlink="Repairing Synthetics" link="CMUGuideEngSynths"].
